name: val-town
title: Val Town
description: Browse your vals, read their logs and traces, and allow Raycast AI to run the ones you choose
author: KevinBatdorf

commands.name: search-vals
commands.title: Search Vals
commands.subtitle: Val Town
commands.description: Browse your vals and choose which ones Raycast AI can call.

tools.name: list-tools
tools.title: List Val Town Tools
tools.description: The user's callable Val Town tools and the arguments each takes. Call this before running any val of theirs.

tools.name: execute-tool
tools.title: Execute Val Town Tool
tools.description: Run one of the user's Val Town tools. Use it whenever the user's request matches a tool's description from list-tools — running them is what they are for. Never guess a name or argument.

tools.name: get-val-info
tools.title: Get Val Town Val Info
tools.description: Read a val's files and source. Only when the source itself matters, such as debugging a failing tool.

tools.name: read-val-blobs
tools.title: Read Val Town Blobs
tools.description: List or read a val's blob storage. Use it to answer questions about a val's stored data without running the val.

tools.name: get-val-runs
tools.title: Get Val Town Runs
tools.description: A val's recent executions with their logs and errors, from the last hour. Use it when a run failed or the user asks what a val has been doing.

tools.name: load-skill
tools.title: Load Val Town Skill
tools.description: Load one of the user's Val Town skills: their own guide naming which vals to call and how. Only when the user explicitly asks to load or use a skill.

ai.instructions: The user's vals are capabilities they set up to be used. Call list-tools, and when the request matches what a val's description says it does, call execute-tool with that val — do not ask first and do not just offer: each val's own confirmation setting already guards anything sensitive. Only a question about the collection itself, like what tools the user has, ends at list-tools. Never invent a val name or an argument.
